Package de.schladebeck.fx.grid

package de.schladebeck.fx.grid

A JavaFX table control for tables of any size. Grid paints all cells into one canvas, so its node count stays the same for ten cells or 100 billion, and only the visible cells cost time.

Getting started

ListGridModel<Person> people = new ListGridModel<Person>()
        .column("Name", Person::name)
        .column("Salary", Person::salary);
people.setAll(loadPeople());          // from any thread

Grid grid = new Grid(people);
grid.getColumn(1).setRenderer(CellRenderers.number("#,##0.00")).setMinWidth(90);
grid.setCellContextMenuFactory(cell -> new ContextMenu(new MenuItem("Open " + cell.value())));

The data comes from any GridModel; de.schladebeck.fx.grid.model has ready-made ones for lists, functions, paged sources and trees. A TreeGrid shows a tree.

Rows and columns

Rows and columns each have a view order (as shown) and a model order (as in the data). Rows are filtered (Grid.setRowFilter(IntPredicate)) and sorted by one or more columns (Grid.sort(java.util.List), Shift+click on a header); columns are hidden and moved (GridColumn.setVisible(boolean), Grid.moveColumn(int, int)). Positions such as the selection and Grid.cellAt(double, double) use view indices; configuration and data use model indices. Grid.viewToModelRow(int) and its relatives convert.

A GridColumn holds a column's width and limits, visibility, renderer, header style and renderer, comparator, converter and a prototype value for fitting the width before data arrives. Grid.getColumn(String) finds a column by name; Grid.columnGroupsProperty() adds rows of group names above the headers. Rows have the row height, or their own from a RowHeightProvider, within Grid.minRowHeightProperty() and Grid.maxRowHeightProperty().

The selection and the focused cell stay with their rows when the view is sorted or filtered and when rows are inserted or deleted; rows inserted or deleted above the viewport do not move what is shown. Sorting or filtering keeps a selection of up to 100,000 rows (whole columns do not count) and clears a larger one; so does inserting or deleting more than 1,000 rows at once in a sorted or filtered view.

Painting

The painting API is in de.schladebeck.fx.grid.render. CellRenderers paint cells straight onto the canvas. The grid picks one per cell: a CellRendererProvider if set, else the column's renderer, else one for the column type or the value's type. CellRenderers has the built-in ones and helpers for formatted and wrapped text. A CellStyleProvider styles single cells: background, text color, font, bold or italic, alignment.

Column headers are painted the same way, by Grid.headerRendererProperty() or a column's own GridColumn.setHeaderRenderer(CellRenderer), styled by GridColumn.setHeaderStyle(CellStyle). The grid keeps room for the sort arrow and paints it after the renderer.

Renderers start from a reset canvas state (see CellRenderer). A renderer that throws leaves its cell empty; the grid logs the first exception of each kind and keeps painting.

CSS reference

Colors, fonts and sizes are CSS properties of the .grid style class. Their defaults come from the Modena theme variables and the inherited font, so a dark theme or a larger font set on .root reaches the grid without any -grid-* property:

.root {
    -fx-base: #3c3f41;
    -fx-control-inner-background: #1e1f22;
    -fx-accent: #2675bf;
    -fx-font-size: 14px;
}
Property Type Default Paints
-grid-font font the inherited -fx-font cell text
-grid-header-font font the inherited -fx-font, bold header text
-grid-text-fill color -fx-text-inner-color cell text, check boxes
-grid-cell-background color -fx-control-inner-background cells
-grid-alternate-cell-background color -fx-control-inner-background-alt every other row
-grid-alternate-column-background color none laid over every other column
-grid-line-color color the cell background, a shade darker or lighter grid lines
-grid-selection-background color a neutral gray, a tint of -fx-accent while focused selected cells
-grid-focus-color color -fx-focus-color focused cell, selection outline, drop marker
-grid-header-background color -fx-base row and column header
-grid-header-text-fill color -fx-text-base-color header text, sort arrow
-grid-row-height size 2em (24 at font size 12) rows without their own height
-grid-header-height size 2.333333em (28) column header
-grid-cell-padding size 0.5em (6) space left and right of the text in a cell

null as -grid-alternate-cell-background turns striping off; a see-through -grid-alternate-column-background such as rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.04) combines with the row stripes. Grid lines are darker than the cells on light themes and lighter on dark ones; the lines after the frozen columns and rows and the header lines are a shade stronger. The focused selection background is light on light themes and dark on dark ones, and is mixed into the headers of selected rows and columns. The focused cell's border and the selection outline are painted only while the grid has the keyboard focus. The defaults are written down in grid.css next to this package; each property also has a Java property of the same name, such as Grid.cellBackgroundProperty().

Values:

  • Colors may use theme variables, derive and ladder, for example -grid-selection-background: derive(-fx-accent, 70%);, or variables of your own defined on .root.
  • Fonts take the shorthand (-grid-font: 14px "Segoe UI";) or single parts (-grid-font-size, -grid-font-family, -grid-font-weight, -grid-font-style); missing parts come from the inherited font.
  • Sizes in em are relative to the grid's font size (-fx-font-size). Setting -fx-font-size on .grid or .root grows the cell font, the header font, the row height and the padding together; a size given only in -grid-font changes the text, not the row height.

Which value wins, strongest first: an inline style (Node.setStyle(String)), a stylesheet of the scene or a parent, a value set in code (such as Grid.setRowHeight(double)), the defaults.

Selectors:

Selector Matches
.grid the grid; its frame is a normal -fx-background-color with insets
.grid:focused the grid while it has the keyboard focus; by default it sets the accent-colored selection
.grid .scroll-bar the two scroll bars, standard JavaFX scroll bars
.grid > .grid-editor the text field of in-place editing
.grid > .grid-editor:invalid the text field while its text cannot be converted to the cell's type 
.grid { -grid-selection-background: #e0e0e0; }
.grid:focused { -grid-selection-background: derive(-fx-accent, 70%); }

CSS is applied before the first layout pass, so getters such as Grid.getFont() return the defaults until the grid is shown. Read them inside renderers, providers and listeners, and give font-dependent sizes in em.

Cells, rows and columns are not nodes, so CSS cannot style them one by one: use a CellStyleProvider for cells, GridColumn.setHeaderStyle(CellStyle) for headers, or a CellRenderer. Context menus and tooltips are standard JavaFX popups with their usual style classes.

Selection, menus and editing

GridSelectionModel holds ranges of cells in one of four SelectionModes. Grid.getSelectedModelRows() and Grid.forEachSelectedCell(Grid.CellVisitor) read the selected data, Grid.focusedModelRowProperty() follows the focused row (for example for a detail form), and Grid.selectModelRow(int) selects a data row wherever it is shown. Ctrl+C copies the selection (Grid.copySelection()).

Right-clicking a cell opens the menu from Grid.cellContextMenuFactoryProperty(). Right-clicking a column header, or Alt+Down, opens the column menu: sorting, fitting, hiding and showing columns, or the menu from Grid.columnMenuFactoryProperty(). Cell tooltips show text that was cut, or the text from Grid.tooltipProviderProperty() and a node from Grid.tooltipGraphicProviderProperty(); they have the style class grid-tooltip. Grid.placeholderProperty() is shown while there are no rows. Built-in texts are English or German, following the default display locale.

A form next to the grid is the recommended way to edit; Grid.setEditable(boolean) turns on in-place editing. The editor converts text with the column's converter, or else numbers in the default locale's format, dates, times, enums and booleans; other types are not edited in place. Text that cannot be converted, or that the model rejects, stays in the editor with a message. A click on a check box or Space toggles it.

Grid.getLayout() captures what a user changed (column order, explicit widths, hidden columns, sort, frozen columns, zoom) as a GridLayout that encodes to a string; Grid.onLayoutChangedProperty() reports changes, for example to save them.

The grid is always laid out left to right, also in a right-to-left scene.

Package Contents

de.schladebeck.fx.grid.model where the data comes from
de.schladebeck.fx.grid.render painting cells and headers: renderers, styles, text measurement

Implementation notes

Grid is a facade over small parts, and so is its skin, which stays in this package to use package-private parts of Grid.

Part Job
internal.ViewRows view rows to model rows: filter, then sort (or let the model sort)
internal.RowSorting the sorts of ViewRows and the default order of values
internal.ColumnLayout column order as runs of model columns, visibility, widths and limits
internal.IndexMap the view to model mapping of the rows; the identity needs no arrays
internal.Spans positions of rows and of columns: a default size plus only the exceptions
internal.TextFitter text widths from character advances cached per font; cuts and wraps text
ColumnSettings per-column settings besides layout (header style, comparator, ...), only where set
RendererRegistry the default renderer choice per cell, with a small fixed cache
GridSkin the nodes, layout, scroll bars, row positions, auto-fit, one repaint per pulse
GridGeometry all viewport math, captured once per layout pass and shared by painting and input
GridPainter paints from the geometry through one reused CellContext; measures on a hidden canvas
GridBehavior mouse, keyboard, scroll, zoom and auto-scroll
ColumnMenu, Texts the built-in column menu and the translated texts
CellEditor, ValueParser the in-place editor and its default text conversion
AccessibleCell the placeholders for assistive technology

A frame: model events, scrolling and property changes only mark the skin dirty and request a layout pass. The layout pass fits columns if needed, updates the geometry and the scroll bars, and repaints the canvas once. The painter clears the canvas and paints the scrolled cells, then the frozen columns, the row header and the column header on top. Within a region it paints all backgrounds, then the renderers column by column, then the lines, so the canvas changes state rarely. Nothing is clipped: text is shortened or wrapped to fit, and later regions cover what scrolled under them.

Memory and time do not grow with the model size: rows and columns that keep their defaults are not stored, and only visible cells are asked for values. Sorting and filtering rows are the exceptions; they need an index array of all rows.
